ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As illustrated, in square $ABCD$ with side length $AB=2$, point $P$ is located on side $AB$ (not coinciding with $A$ or $B$). A square $PBEF$ is constructed inside square $ABCD$ with $PB$ as a side, intersecting side $BC$ at point $E$. Lines $DF$ and $CF$ are drawn. When $\triangle CDF$ is an isosceles triangle with $D$ as the apex, what is the length of $PB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Connect BF,\\
Quadrilaterals ABCD, PBEF are squares, AB=2,\\
$\therefore$ Points B, F, D are collinear, CD=AB=2, $\angle A=90^\circ$\\
$\therefore$ $BD=\sqrt{AD^{2}+AB^{2}}=\sqrt{2^{2}+2^{2}}=2\sqrt{2}$\\
$\because$ $\triangle CDF$ is an isosceles triangle with D as the vertex,\\
$\therefore$FD=CD=2, BF=BD-FC=$2\sqrt{2}-2$,\\
$\because$2PB$^{2}$=BF$^{2}$\\
$\therefore$ $PB=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}BF=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\left(2\sqrt{2}-2\right)=\boxed{2-\sqrt{2}}$;

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the large square is ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left; P is on the bottom side AB and close to B. With PB as a side, the small square PBEF is constructed inside the large square, where E is on the right side BC, and F is the upper-left vertex of the small square. DF and CF are drawn in the figure; when the diagonal BF of the small square is additionally connected, BF and the diagonal DB of the large square are on the same straight line. Reasoning: It is known that ABCD is a square with side length 2, so CD=2, and the diagonal of the large square BD=√(AB^2+AD^2)=√(2^2+2^2)=2√2. Also BF is the diagonal of the small square PBEF; if PB is its side length, then BF=PB√2. Therefore PB=(2√2-2)/√2=2-√2.
